<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Management Performance and Financial Conditions</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left">
<A name="C16070102"></A>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>(1)&nbsp;Outline of Operations and Business Results</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>&#091;Effects of the Great East Japan Earthquake on Komatsu Group&#146;s Business Operations and Responses&#093;</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">During the fiscal year, ended March&nbsp;31, 2011, i.e., from April&nbsp;1, 2010 to March&nbsp;31, 2011, the Great
East Japan Earthquake and the subsequent tsunami brought about very extensive damages, especially
in the Tohoku and northern Kanto regions of Japan. Immediately after this tragic disaster, the
Komatsu Group checked the safety of its employees and their families, worked to secure their
safety, and made all-out efforts in transporting relief items to disaster-stricken employees and
their families. The Komatsu Group also focused its efforts to recover operations of affected
plants, suppliers and other business bases.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">With respect to production, the buildings and facilities of some plants of the Komatsu Group
were damaged but we quickly worked to repair them. For our suppliers, many employees from the
Production and Procurement divisions went to their facilities and worked together with suppliers&#146;
employees on quick repair of their facilities. As a result of these efforts, all our affected
plants resumed production by the end of March, while we are still experiencing uncertain
procurement conditions for some electronic parts of construction equipment as well as electric
power supply.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">Our sales and service operations were seriously affected by the tsunami. At some bases located
along the Pacific Ocean side of the Tohoku region, their buildings, facilities and construction
equipment were washed away. While it will take some time for us to recover those full-scale
operations, soon after the devastation brought by the tsunami we restarted our maintenance and
repair service for construction equipment, which is indispensable for the restoration and
reconstruction of the affected regions by our other bases nearby.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">As an effort within our best capacity to offer equipment and materials needed in the affected
regions, we have decided on a JPY800&nbsp;million worth assistance action plan centering on
free-of-charge lending of our own construction equipment, forklift trucks, temporary housing and
power generators. We have delivered them per the requests of local governments.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">It is projected that reconstruction work will last for a long time. We recognize the
importance of producing construction equipment, an indispensable tool of restoration and
reconstruction, promptly delivering them to the needed areas, and continuing our maintenance and
repair operation to ensure trouble-free use of equipment, while continuing to work to normalize our
operations.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>&#091;Outline of Operations and Business Results&#093;</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Komatsu Ltd. (&#147;Company&#148;) and its consolidated subsidiaries (together &#147;Komatsu&#148;) embarked on the
Global Teamwork for Tomorrow mid-range management plan for three years starting in the fiscal year
under review, which emphasize (1)&nbsp;promotion of ICT applications to products and parts, (2)&nbsp;further
advancement of environmental friendliness and safety in machine performance, (3)&nbsp;expansion of sales
and service operations in Strategic Markets, and (4)&nbsp;promotion of continuous Kaizen (improvement)
by strengthening workplace capability.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">In the first year of the ongoing mid range plan, demand for construction and mining equipment
remained at a high level in Strategic Markets, especially in China, Asia and Latin America, while
demand recovered and increased from the previous fiscal year in the Traditional Markets of Japan,
North America
and Europe. Demand for industrial machinery also turned toward recovery, reflecting an increased
volume of production of cars in Strategic Markets and growth of the solar cell industry in China
and Asia.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->6<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C16070tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><IMG src="c16070c1607002.gif" alt="(KOMATSU LOGO)">
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">&#091;Markets as Positioned by the Komatsu&#093;
</DIV>

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head --><TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="48%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="50%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>

<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD valign="top"><DIV style="margin-left:0px; text-indent:-0px">Traditional Markets
</DIV></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="left" valign="top">Japan, North America and Europe</TD>
</TR>
<TR valign="bottom" style="padding-top: 1px">
    <TD valign="top"><DIV style="margin-left:0px; text-indent:-0px">Strategic Markets
</DIV></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="left" valign="top">China, Latin America, Asia, Oceania, Africa, Middle East and CIS</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body --></TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">During the fiscal year under review, Komatsu recorded consolidated net sales of JPY1,843.1
billion (USD22,206&nbsp;million, at USD1=JPY83), up 28.7% from the previous fiscal year. While the
Japanese currency appreciated sharply against the U.S. dollar, Euro and Renminbi from the previous
fiscal year and we incurred a loss resulting from the damages by the Great East Japan Earthquake
and the subsequent tsunami, we made sizable gains by expanding the volume of sales and continuing
structural reform efforts, such as the realization of selling prices and the improvement of
production costs. Specifically, operating income reached JPY222.9&nbsp;billion (USD2,686&nbsp;million),
registering an increase of 232.6% from the previous fiscal year, and operating income ratio
advanced to 12.1%, an improvement of 7.4&nbsp;percentage points. Income before income taxes and equity
in earnings of affiliated companies increased by 238.3% to JPY219.8&nbsp;billion (USD2,648&nbsp;million). Net
income attributable to Komatsu Ltd. totaled JPY150.7&nbsp;billion (USD1,816&nbsp;million), recording an
improvement of 349.2%.
</DIV>

</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><U><B>Construction, Mining and Utility Equipment</B></U>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Komatsu expanded consolidated net sales of construction, mining and utility equipment by 27.4% to
JPY1,615.6&nbsp;billion (USD19,466&nbsp;million) by steadfastly capitalizing on global demand recovery.
During the fiscal year under review, Komatsu continued to focus its efforts especially to expand
production capacity and reinforce product support operation by anticipating the mid to long-range
growth of Strategic Markets. To accelerate sales of hybrid hydraulic excavators, which offer
improved fuel consumption and CO<SUB style="font-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-bottom">2</SUB> emissions volume, Komatsu tooled up the production of
new HB205 and HB215LC hybrid hydraulic excavators after changing the forerunner model, introduced
them on the Japanese market and decided to launch them in major markets around the world. With
respect to the utility equipment business, consisting of forklift trucks and mini construction
equipment, the Company decided to merge Komatsu Utility Co., Ltd. in order to speed up the pace of
strengthening its business in overseas markets, further improve their product competitiveness and
product development capability, and reinforce human resource development.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Japan</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">While public works began to decline in the second half period of the fiscal year under review,
private-sector capital investment remained strong. Against this backdrop, demand for construction
equipment headed for recovery centering on the rental equipment segment, and sales improved from
the previous fiscal year in Japan. In December&nbsp;2010, Komatsu launched sales of new HB205 and
HB215LC hybrid hydraulic excavators in Japan before overseas markets, received great responses from
their customers and enjoyed good sales.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Note: For effects of the Great East Japan Earthquake on Komatsu&#146;s business operations, see on page
6.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Americas</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In North America, while the U.S. housing starts remained sluggish, overall demand for equipment
turned for recovery, supported by strong demand in the rental equipment and mining industries. In
this market environment, Komatsu continued to promote the zero inventory of distributors campaign
and worked to improve their financial strength. Komatsu also advanced preparation for the market
introduction of products compliant to new emission control regulations. In Latin America, demand
for equipment remained strong in mining, civil engineering, agricultural and forestry sectors in
Brazil, the largest Latin American market. In Chile where demand for mining equipment grew sharply,
Komatsu strengthened its sales and product support capabilities for the mining industry. As a
result, sales increased from the previous fiscal year.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->8<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C16070tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><IMG src="c16070c1607002.gif" alt="(KOMATSU LOGO)">
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Europe &#038; CIS</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Demand for construction equipment headed for recovery mainly in major markets such as Germany, the
United Kingdom and France. While demand recovered in these markets, Komatsu worked to strengthen
its product support capability and expand sales of parts by teaming up with its distributors. As a
result, sales improved from the previous fiscal year.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">In CIS, demand for large equipment grew, centering on use for coal and gold mining as well as
energy development, and sales improved from the previous fiscal year. To seize on the mid to
long-range demand for mining equipment, Komatsu strengthened its production and product support
capabilities by commencing production at Komatsu Manufacturing Rus, LLC. in June last year and
opening the Kuzbass Support Center in Siberia.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>China</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Demand for construction and mining equipment remained strong, reflecting thriving demand in the
mining industry coupled with advancement of infrastructure development and urbanization, especially
in inner China. Particularly by steadfastly capitalizing on demand, which followed the Chinese New
Year in February this year, Komatsu registered record-high sales in China.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">In tandem with this market expansion, Komatsu worked to expand its production, sales and
product support capabilities, especially by establishing Komatsu China Mining Limited to engage in
sales and product support for major mining companies, constructing the new plant of Komatsu
(Changzhou) Construction Machinery Corp., opening the KC Techno Center, and training service
engineers in the special training course at Shandong Jiaotong University.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Asia &#038; Oceania</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In Indonesia, the largest market of Southeast Asia, demand for mining equipment continued to
expand, while demand for construction equipment remained strong in the civil engineering,
agriculture and forestry sectors. Demand was also strong in India, Thailand, Malaysia and some
other countries. In Australia, some mining companies experienced adverse effects of the flood in
shipment of their commodities in the second half period, but overall demand for mining equipment
remained firm. Under such market conditions, sales accelerated in Asia, resulting in an increase in
sales from the previous fiscal year in Asia &#038; Oceania. In Southeast Asia, Komatsu concerted efforts
to introduce KOMTRAX (Komatsu Machine Tracking System)-installed standard construction equipment
to more regions. In Australia, Komatsu continued to reinforce sales and product support operations,
including the reorganization of Komatsu Australia Pty Ltd in August last year to further strengthen
its capabilities as a distributor.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Middle East &#038; Africa</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">While political and social conditions have continued to be unstable in some countries, demand for
equipment remained firm, particularly in the mining sector. As a result, sales improved from the
previous fiscal year. Komatsu is expecting market expansion into the future as accompanied by the
development of new mines and the recovery of infrastructure development. In Africa, Komatsu
continued its efforts to strengthen its product support capability by adding a new training center
to foster the growth of service engineers of distributors.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->9<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C16070tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><IMG src="c16070c1607002.gif" alt="(KOMATSU LOGO)">
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><U><B>Industrial Machinery and Others</B></U>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the industrial machinery and others business, Komatsu boosted sales of wire saws for use in
slicing silicon ingots, as capital investment remained brisk in Asia, centering on China, for the
solar cell market. As a result, sales expanded by 39.5% from the previous fiscal year, to JPY227.4
billion (USD2,740&nbsp;million). Orders received for large presses and other machinery upturned for
growth, as the automobile manufacturing industry began capital investment in China, India, Brazil
and some other countries.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">To further enhance the competitive strength of its industrial machinery
business under such market conditions, following the reorganization of press business in April last
year, the Company decided to merge Komatsu NTC Ltd. and Komatsu Machinery Corporation into a single
entity and to absorb Komatsu Engineering Corp. Concerning the merger of Komatsu NTC and Komatsu
Machinery, as both companies mainly engage in machine tools for the automobile manufacturing
industry as well as semiconductor manufacturing equipment, Komatsu is going to focus its efforts to
converge their technologies and know-how to develop and produce new products for broader lineups as
well as those designed to meet next-generation technological applications. With respect to the
absorption of Komatsu Engineering, as it has a leading-expertise in systems engineering, the
Company is going to apply that expertise to its manufacturing engineering, development and design
operations.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">Furthermore, Komatsu NTC Ltd. has built a new plant in order to expand its production capacity
of wire saws against the backdrop of expanding its share of the solar cell market.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>&#091;Projections for the Fiscal Year Ending March&nbsp;31, 2012&#093;</B>
</DIV>



<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; margin-left: 4%">(From April&nbsp;1, 2011 to March&nbsp;31, 2012)
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the construction, mining and utility equipment business, demand is on a recovery track in
Traditional Markets of North America and Europe in addition to the strong growth of Strategic
Markets. Furthermore, as mining activities are brisk for the production of commodities, we are
projecting that demand for mining equipment will continue into the next fiscal year. In the
industrial machinery and others business, the press and machine tool markets are recovering, while
demand for wire saws should remain strong. Komatsu will unfailingly capitalize on these market
expansions and thereby expand not only sales of new equipment but also sales in the entire value
chain, including parts sales and service revenues. At the same time, Komatsu will continue to
improve selling prices and production costs. As a result, Komatsu is projecting that both
consolidated sales and profits will increase for the fiscal year ending March&nbsp;31, 2012 as shown
below.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">Nevertheless, Komatsu needs to continue to closely monitor a number of problems caused by the
Great East Japan Earthquake, such as power supply, recovery of production at suppliers, aftershocks
and the crippled nuclear plant in Fukushima Prefecture. With respect to extraordinary demand in
restoration and reconstruction of the devastated regions, a large portion of what will be done
remains uncertain, and thus it is not incorporated in the projected business results.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->10<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>(2)&nbsp;Financial Conditions</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">As of March&nbsp;31, 2011, total assets increased by JPY190&nbsp;billion from the previous fiscal year-end,
to JPY2,149.1&nbsp;billion (USD25,893&nbsp;million), mainly due to increased receivables resulting from
expanded sales. Interest-bearing debt declined by JPY42.3&nbsp;billion from the previous fiscal
year-end, to JPY544.0&nbsp;billion (USD6,555&nbsp;million). Komatsu Ltd. shareholders&#146; equity increased by
JPY89.8&nbsp;billion from the previous fiscal year-end, to JPY923.8&nbsp;billion (USD11,131&nbsp;million). As a
result, Komatsu Ltd. shareholders&#146; equity ratio increased by 0.4 points from the previous fiscal
year-end, to 43.0%. Net debt-to-equity ratio* was 0.50 compared to 0.60 as of the previous fiscal
year-end.
</DIV>



<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">
<TR style="font-size: 6pt">
    <TD width="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="96%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">*</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Net debt-to-equity ratio = (Interest-bearing debt &#151; Cash and cash dividends &#151; Time deposits) /
Komatsu Ltd. shareholders&#146; equity</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">For the fiscal year under review, net cash provided by operating activities decreased by
JPY31.7&nbsp;billion from the previous fiscal year, to JPY150.4&nbsp;billion (USD1,812&nbsp;million), mainly due
to expanded working capital. Net cash used in investing activities increased by JPY15.5&nbsp;billion, to
JPY88.5&nbsp;billion (USD1,066&nbsp;million), largely due to investments made to expand production capacity
in Japan and overseas. Net cash used in financing activities declined by JPY59.9&nbsp;billion from the
previous fiscal year, to JPY56.3&nbsp;billion (USD679&nbsp;million), mainly due to decreased repayments on
debt. As a result, cash and cash equivalents, as of March&nbsp;31, 2011, totaled JPY84.2&nbsp;billion
(USD1,015&nbsp;million), registering an increase of JPY1.7&nbsp;billion from the previous fiscal year-end.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; margin-left: 4%">Cash flow indexes are described below.

<DIV align="left">
<A name="C16070104"></A>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>(3)&nbsp;Basic Policy for Redistribution of Profits and Dividends for the Fiscal Year under Review and
Next Fiscal Year</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Komatsu is building a sound financial position as well as flexible and agile corporate strengths to
increase its corporate value. Concerning cash dividends to shareholders, the Company maintains the
policy of redistributing profits by considering consolidated business results and continuing stable
dividends. Specifically, the Company has set the goal of a consolidated payout ratio of 20% or
higher. Further, it maintains the policy of not decreasing dividends, as long as the consolidated
payout ratio does not surpass 40%.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">After reviewing the business results for the fiscal year under review as well as current and
future business prospects, the Company is planning to set the fiscal year-end dividend at JPY20 per
share. (The Company plans to propose this amount to the 142<SUP style="font-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">nd</SUP> ordinary general meeting
of shareholders scheduled for June&nbsp;22, 2011.) Annual cash dividends for the year under review,
including the interim dividend of JPY18 per share, amount to JPY38 per share (an increase of JPY22
from annual cash dividends for the previous fiscal year). This amount translates into a
consolidated payout ratio of 24%.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">Regarding the fiscal year ending March&nbsp;31, 2012, the Company plans to set the annual cash
dividends per share at JPY42, an increase of JPY4, compared to JPY38 for the fiscal year ended
March&nbsp;31, 2011.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Cautionary Statement</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The announcement set forth herein contains forward-looking statements which reflect management&#146;s
current views with respect to certain future events, including expected financial position,
operating results, and business strategies. These statements can be identified by the use of terms
such as &#147;will,&#148; &#147;believes,&#148; &#147;should,&#148; &#147;projects&#148; and similar terms and expressions that identify
future events or expectations. Actual results may differ materially from those projected, and the
events and results of such forward-looking assumptions cannot be assured.
Factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from those predicted by such
forward-looking statements include, but are not limited to, unanticipated changes in demand for
Komatsu&#146;s principal products, owing to changes in the economic conditions in Komatsu&#146;s principal
markets; changes in exchange rates or the impact of increased competition; unanticipated cost or
delays encountered in achieving Komatsu&#146;s objectives with respect to globalized product sourcing
and new Information Technology tools; uncertainties as to the results of Komatsu&#146;s research and
development efforts and its ability to access and protect certain intellectual property rights;
and, the impact of regulatory changes and accounting principles and practices.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<A name="C16070106"></A>
</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Management Policy</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left">
<A name="C16070107"></A>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>(1)&nbsp;Basic Management Policy</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The cornerstone of Komatsu&#146;s management is commitment to Quality and Reliability for maximization
of its corporate value. This commitment is not limited to delivering safe and innovative products
and services which incorporate the viewpoints of customers. Komatsu is continuing its efforts to
enhance the Quality and Reliability of all organizations, businesses, employees and management of
the entire Komatsu Group. It is the top management task of Komatsu to continue improving the
Quality and Reliability of all these, year after year.
</DIV>
<DIV align="left">
<A name="C16070108"></A>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>(2)&nbsp;Mid to Long-Range Management Plan and Issues Ahead</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Komatsu&#146;s production and procurement remain vulnerable to being affected by such conditions as the
electric power supply, suppliers&#146; recovery of operations, aftershocks and the crippled nuclear
plant in Fukushima Prefecture. We will continue our all-out efforts to stabilize production and
procurement as we monitor the conditions very carefully.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">Concerning the restoration of the regions devastated by the Great East Japan Earthquake, we
created the Tohoku Operation Department in Sendai City, Miyagi Prefecture. The Department will
ensure dynamic decision-making operations in the affected regions, provide for the smooth
transportation of construction equipment, forklift trucks, temporary housing materials, and spare
parts for equipment, and reinforce our service operations.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">Looking at our global group-wide business environment, Strategic Markets are steadily
expanding in the construction and mining equipment business. We are projecting that the economic
growth of countries in Strategic Markets will play the role of driving the demand for equipment. In
the industrial machinery and others business, we are also anticipating that demand will continue to
grow, as the volume of automobile production is increasing, especially in Strategic Markets.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">Komatsu draws its strengths especially from ICT applications, in-house development and
production capabilities of key components, global sales and service networks, and flexible
procurement and manufacturing operations. In the new mid-range management plan, &#147;Global Teamwork
for Tomorrow,&#148; with the goals set for the fiscal year ending March&nbsp;31, 2013, we are working to
further refine our strengths by focusing our efforts on the following activities of importance and
will steadfastly generate results. We will also continue our efforts to disseminate and anchor The
KOMATSU Way, as all employees of Komatsu engage in Kaizen (improvement)&nbsp;activities in their own
work. In addition, we will focus our efforts on our brand management activities designed to further
enrich the relationship with our customers for mutual growth with them and foster the growth of
employees who are needed for our global business expansion.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Activities of Importance in the &#147;Global Teamwork for Tomorrow&#148;</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">1) Promotion of ICT Applications to Products and Parts
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">We have built on our record of ICT applications mainly in the domain of construction and mining
equipment with the KOMTRAX for construction equipment, the AHS (Autonomous Haulage System) for dump
trucks in large-scale mines and other systems. We will continue to apply leading-edge ICT to
machine management, machine control, and construction site management in order to enhance our
product competitiveness. We will also proactively promote ICT applications to our industrial
machinery and forklift trucks. Furthermore, we are going to advance our utilization of a variety of
information obtained from the KOMTRAX to improve customers&#146; productivity and our sales and
production planning.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">2) Further Advancement of Environmental Friendliness and Safety in Machine Performance
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">To help our customers reduce CO<SUB style="font-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-bottom">2</SUB> emission volume from their equipment, we are going to
advance our hybrid, HST (hydrostatic transmission) and motor-driven technologies for construction
equipment and forklift trucks and our AC Servo technology for presses. With respect to hybrid
hydraulic excavators, we are preparing for worldwide launchings of new HB205 and HB215LC models. By
combining our in-house development and production of key components, such as engines, hydraulic
equipment and control systems with leading-edge technologies, we are continuing our efforts to
develop products to meet new emissions control regulations in Japan, North America and Europe and
to ensure their smooth market introduction. In the domain of mining equipment, we have already
introduced the AHS to mines in Chile and Australia, and we are going to further refine the
performance and safety of the AHS. We are also going to generate steady results in the Biodiesel
Fuel Project which we started in the previous fiscal year.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">3) Expansion of Sales and Service Operations in Strategic Markets
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In Strategic Markets and in the domain of mining equipment, which both have high growth potential,
we are going to make a difference from competitors by not only supplying products which feature
superior QCDS (quality, costs, delivery and safety) but also enhancing the operating rates of
customers&#146; equipment through quick and responsive delivery of parts and service. To this end, we
are going to upgrade our sales and service capabilities by developing and strengthening
distributorships, expanding service support bases, reinforcing parts and Reman businesses and
supporting customers through ICT applications. Also, in the domain of industrial machinery and
forklift trucks, we are going to promote more synergy effects with the construction equipment
business, and improve sales and service networks in response to an expanding weight on Strategic
Markets centering on China.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><IMG src="c16070c1607002.gif" alt="(KOMATSU LOGO)">
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">4) Promotion of Continuous Kaizen (Improvement) by Strengthening Workplace Capability.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">While the growth of emerging economies offers us a great chance to expand our business, we need to
expect new competition with companies of emerging economies in addition to conventional
competition. To win this global mega competition, it is important for us to continuously refine our
capability to meet the changes
and sharpen our cost competitiveness, as we promote our efforts for growth upheld in the mid-range
management plan. To this end, it is absolutely necessary for us to have the power to demonstrate
workplace capability and adaptability, i.e., the power to continue our Kaizen (improvement)
activities. With this workplace capability and effective ICT utilization, we are going to further
heighten our operational flexibility of global manufacturing operations, substantially reduce
production costs, and maximize logistics. We are also continuing our efforts to reform and
streamline our administrative work. Through these Kaizen (improvement)&nbsp;activities, we are going to
further enhance our workplace capability and promote human resource development.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Based on the belief that &#147;our corporate value is the total sum of trust given to us by society and
all our stakeholders,&#148; Komatsu are further strengthening our corporate governance to ensure sound
and transparent management, while improving management efficiency. Being committed to promoting
thorough compliance, we will also ensure that all employees share The KOMATSU Way. In addition to
improving our business performance, we will facilitate both the development of corporate strength
and the achievement of social responsibility in a well balanced manner.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->17<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Giving the Board of Directors the Authority to Issue Stock Acquisition Rights as &#147;Stock-Based<BR>
Remuneration&#148; to Employees of the Company and Directors of Major Subsidiaries of the Company</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Komatsu Ltd. (hereinafter &#147;Company&#148;) hereby announces that at the meeting of the Board of Directors
held on April&nbsp;27, 2011, the Company resolved to propose an agendum to the 142nd Ordinary General
Meeting of Shareholders which will be held on June&nbsp;22, 2011, to give the Company&#146;s Board of
Directors the authority to issue Stock Acquisition Rights as &#147;stock-based remuneration&#148; to
employees of the Company and Directors of major subsidiaries of the Company in accordance with the
provisions of Articles 236, 238, and 239 of the Corporation Act. See below for details.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">&#091;Description&#093;
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">1.</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Reasons for Necessity of Issuing the Stock Acquisition Rights on Preferential Terms and
Conditions</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The Company would like to grant Stock Acquisition Rights to employees of the Company and to the
Directors of major subsidiaries of the Company without consideration not only for the purposes of
raising their morale and their motivation to contribute to the improvement of the consolidated
performance of the Company, but also for the purpose of clarifying their incentive to enhance the
long-term corporate value of the Company by fostering the same perspective on earnings with the
shareholders. The number of Stock Acquisition Rights to be granted without consideration shall be
determined based on the Company&#146;s consolidated performance, as with the payment criteria of the
&#147;stock-based remuneration&#148; for the Directors of the Company.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">2.</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Details of the Stock Acquisition Rights and the Maximum Number of Such Rights that the Board
of Directors Can Decide to Issue within the Scope of Authority Granted by a Resolution at this
Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">(1)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The maximum number of the Stock Acquisition Rights for which the terms and conditions of the
issue can be determined based on the authority granted by this Ordinary General Meeting of
Shareholders</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The maximum number of Stock Acquisition Rights to be issued under the conditions described in 2.
(3)&nbsp;below shall be 2,529 units.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 8pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The maximum number of common stock to be issued upon the exercise of the Stock Acquisition
Rights shall be 252,900 shares, and if the Number of Shares Granted (defined below) subject to
Stock Acquisition Rights is adjusted as provided for in 2. (3)&nbsp;below, the maximum number of
common stock to be issued shall be the number obtained by multiplying
the above mentioned maximum number of the Stock Acquisition Rights by the adjusted number
of shares in connection with the Stock Acquisition Rights.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV><P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The Company may issue Stock Acquisition Rights in question without consideration.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">(3)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Details of the Stock Acquisition Rights to be issued on the basis of the authority granted by
this Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">1)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Type and number of shares to be issued upon the exercise of Stock Acquisition Rights
The shares to be issued for the Stock Acquisition Rights shall be common stock, and the
number of shares subject to one (1)&nbsp;Stock Acquisition Right (hereinafter &#147;Number of Shares
Granted&#148;) shall be 100 shares. However, after the resolution date of this agendum at the
142nd Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (hereinafter &#147;Resolution Date&#148;), if the
Company effects a stock split of its common stock (including allotment of common stock to
shareholders without consideration; the same applies hereinafter) or effects a stock
consolidation, the Number of Shares Granted subject to one (1)&nbsp;Stock Acquisition Right shall
be adjusted proportionately, in accordance with the ratio of the stock split or the stock
consolidation in question. Also, if it is necessary to adjust the Number of Shares Granted
after the Resolution Date for reasons other than the aforementioned reasons, the Company
shall adjust the Number of Shares Granted in connection with the aforementioned Stock
Acquisition Rights to the extent reasonable.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 8pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Fractions of less than one (1)&nbsp;share resulting from the foregoing adjustment shall be
rounded down.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">2)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Amount of assets to be paid upon exercise of the Stock Acquisition Rights</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The amount of assets to be paid upon exercise of the Stock Acquisition Rights shall be JPY 1
per each one (1)&nbsp;share to be transferred upon exercise of the Stock Acquisition Rights,
multiplied by the Number of Shares to be transferred.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">3)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Exercise period for the Stock Acquisition Rights</DIV></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 8pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">From August&nbsp;1, 2014 to July&nbsp;31, 2019</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">4)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Matters concerning the increase in paid-in capital and capital surplus in the event of
issuance of shares upon the exercise of the Stock Acquisition Rights</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="12%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">i.</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The amount of paid-in capital increase in the event of the issuance of shares upon
the exercise of the Stock Acquisition Rights shall be one half of the maximum amount of
capital increase, calculated in accordance with Article&nbsp;17, Paragraph&nbsp;1 of the Regulations
for Corporation Accounting. Fractions less than one (1)&nbsp;yen resulting from the
calculation shall be rounded up.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="12%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">ii.</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">An increase in the capital surplus in the event of the issuance of shares upon
exercise of the Stock Acquisition Rights shall be the amount obtainable by subtracting the
amount of the paid-in capital increase from the maximum amount of the capital increase, as
set forth in 4) i. above.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">


<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt"><TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">



</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">6)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Provisions pertaining to acquisition of the Stock Acquisition Rights by the Company</DIV></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 8pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The Stock Acquisition Rights do not contain the provisions pertaining to the acquisition by the
Company.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">7)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Conditions for exercising the Stock Acquisition Rights</DIV></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 8pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">If a holder of Stock Acquisition Rights who is a Director, Corporate Auditor or employee of the
Company, or Director, Corporate Auditor or employee of an affiliate of the Company, loses his
or her all respective states set above, that person is able to exercise the Stock Acquisition
Rights only within a period of three years from the date they lost their position; provided,
however, that the period shall not exceed the exercise period for the Stock Acquisition Rights
described at 3)above, and the other terms and conditions concerning the exercise of Stock
Acquisition Rights shall be decided at a meeting of the Company&#146;s Board of Directors.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">8)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">In the event where the Company engages in any merger (limited to a case where the Company
ceases to exist as the result of the merger), a corporate split in which a division of the
Company is merged into an existing company, a corporate split in which a division of the
Company is spun off to establish a new company (for both, limited to cases where the Company
is split up), or an exchange or transfer of shares (for both, limited to cases where the
Company becomes a fully-owned subsidiary) (hereinafter collectively &#147;Restructuring Actions&#148;),
each person holding the remaining Stock Acquisition Rights at the time the Restructuring
Actions take effect (hereinafter &#147;Remaining Stock Acquisition Rights&#148;) shall be granted the
Stock Acquisition Rights of the relevant stock companies prescribed in Article&nbsp;236, Paragraph
1, Item&nbsp;8, (a)&nbsp;through (e)&nbsp;of the Corporation Act (hereinafter &#147;Reorganized Company&#148;), in
accordance with the conditions set forth below. In this event, the Remaining Stock
Acquisition Rights shall become null and void and new Stock Acquisition Rights in the
Reorganized Company shall be issued. However, the new Stock Acquisition Rights shall be
granted only if provisions for granting them in accordance with the following conditions
(i&#151;viii) are included as conditions in a merger agreement (in which the Company is merged
into a Reorganized Company or a Reorganized Company is established as the result of the
merger), a corporate split agreement in which a division of the Company is merged into a
Reorganized Company, a plan for a corporate split in which a division of the Company is spun
off to establish a Reorganized Company, a share exchange agreement or a plan for transfer of shares.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="12%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">i.</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Number of the Stock Acquisition Rights of a Reorganized Company to be granted</DIV></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 8pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="12%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">At the time the Restructuring Actions take effect, each holder of the Remaining Stock
Acquisition Rights shall be granted an identical number of the Stock Acquisition Rights of
the Reorganized Company.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="12%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">ii.</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Type of shares of the Reorganized Company to be issued for the Stock Acquisition
Rights</DIV></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 8pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="12%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Type of shares subject to the Stock Acquisition Rights shall be common stock of the
Reorganized Company.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">iii.</TD>

    <TD style="font-size: 8pt">&nbsp;</TD>

    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">The number of shares shall be determined in accordance with 1) above, after taking into
consideration the conditions or other factors concerning the Restructuring Actions.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">At the 141st Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders, held on June&nbsp;23, 2010, it was approved that
the total amount of remuneration in the form of Stock Acquisition Rights to be granted to the
Directors of the Company as the &#147;stock-based remuneration&#148; for each fiscal year shall be no more
than JPY 360&nbsp;million (of which, up to JPY50&nbsp;million shall be allocated for Outside Directors) and
that the maximum number of Stock Acquisition Rights so issued to the Directors of the Company as
the &#147;stock-based remuneration&#148; in the one year period after the date of each Ordinary General
Meeting of Shareholders shall be 2,390 units (of which, 330 units may be the maximum number to be
allocated for Outside Directors).
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The Company plans to resolve issuance and allocation of the foregoing Stock Acquisition Rights
within the above limits at a meeting of the Board of Directors to be held in this fiscal year.
</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Payment of Cash Dividends for the Fiscal Year Ended March&nbsp;31, 2011</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the Board meeting held on April&nbsp;27, 2011, the Board of Directors of Komatsu Ltd.
(hereinafter the &#147;Company,&#148; President &#038; CEO: Kunio Noji) made a resolution that the Company is
going to propose the following cash dividends from retained earnings as of March&nbsp;31, 2011, the date
of record, to the 142<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">nd </SUP>ordinary general meeting of shareholders.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><U><B>2. Reason for the Revision</B></U>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Komatsu is building a sound financial position and flexible and agile corporate strengths to
increase its corporate value. Concerning cash dividends to shareholders, the Company maintains the
policy of redistributing profits by considering consolidated business results and continuing stable
dividends. Specifically, the Company has set the goal of a consolidated payout ratio of 20% or
higher, and maintains the policy of not decreasing dividends, as long as a consolidated payout
ratio will not surpass 40%.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">For the fiscal year ended March&nbsp;31, 2011, both operations of construction, mining and utility
equipment and industrial machinery and others improved business results, and generated &#165;150,752
million for net income attributable to the Company.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">With respect to annual cash dividends for the fiscal year ended March&nbsp;31, 2011, while
following its basic policy for redistribution of profits, the Company plans to pay &#165;38 per share,
based on profits which exclude the reform associated expenses above. The consolidated payout ratio
translates into 24% based on profits excluding the reform associated expenses.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">As interim dividends of &#165;18 per share have already been paid, the year-end cash dividends from
retained earnings will be &#165;20 (compared to &#165;18 projected earlier). The Company plans to propose
these cash dividends from retained earnings to the 142<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">nd</SUP> ordinary general meeting of
shareholders scheduled for June&nbsp;22, 2011.
</DIV>
<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Komatsu Announces Restructuring of the Rental Equipment Business in Japan<BR>
(Simplified Absorption-Type Merger of consolidated Subsidiary)</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Komatsu Ltd. (President and CEO: Kunio Noji) announces today that the Board of Directors, at the
Board meeting held on April&nbsp;27, resolved to approve the merger of Komatsu Rental Ltd. (hereinafter
&#147;Komatsu Rental&#148;), a consolidated subsidiary of Komatsu Ltd. as follows.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">As this merger is going to take place between Komatsu Ltd. and a consolidated subsidiary in
the form of simplified absorption, certain matters and descriptions are omitted from the disclosure
below.
</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Description
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><U>1. Purpose of the Merger</U>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">As the ratio of rental equipment used in civil engineering and construction works has grown
steadily in Japan over the years, the Komatsu Group has worked to strengthen its rental and used
equipment business, while engaging in sales of new equipment. The Komatsu Group has positioned the
rental equipment business as its core operation in Japan and thus worked to meet the changing
market environment by proactively applying ICT (Information and Communication Technologies) to the
rental business. However, the Komatsu Group needs to reassess the rental business operation today.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">The planned restructuring calls for a reassessment of the roles of the rental business
conventionally played by Komatsu Rental in the Komatsu Group. Komatsu Ltd. is going to succeed to
the rental equipment assets of Komatsu Rental, while a new wholly owned subsidiary of Komatsu Ltd.
will take over and engage exclusively in the indispensable rental operation for customers on the
Japanese market in order to further improve and streamline customer services.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">At the same time, Komatsu Ltd. will continue to further enhance its position in Strategic
Markets, such as China and Southeast Asia, while expanding the business throughout its entire value
chain.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->1<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">2) Merger method
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In this simplified absorption-type merger of a consolidated subsidiary, Komatsu Ltd. will become
the surviving company, and Komatsu Rental will be dissolved.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">As Komatsu Rental has excessive liabilities, which are believed to be too large for Komatsu
Rental to resolve before the merger, Komatsu Ltd. is going to waive JPY 23&nbsp;billion (planned)&nbsp;its
claims in the form of loans to Komatsu Rental prior to the concerned merger and thereby resolve the
problem of Komatsu Rental&#146;s excessive liabilities.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt; text-indent: 4%">Also prior to the concerned merger, Komatsu Rental will establish a wholly owned, new rental
company, and execute an absorption-type company split with Komatsu Rental becoming the splitting
company and the new rental company becoming the succeeding company. The succeeding company will
succeed to Komatsu Rental&#146;s assets and liabilities (except for rental equipment manufactured by
Komatsu Ltd., some real estate and liabilities related thereto).
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">3) Substance of merger-related allotment of shares
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Komatsu Ltd. owns 79.0% of the total shares of Komatsu Rental and plans to purchase the remaining
shares owned by the other shareholder of Komatsu Rental and to make Komatsu Rental a wholly-owned
subsidiary of Komatsu Ltd. prior to the concerned merger. After acquiring ownership of all shares
of Komatsu Rental, Komatsu Ltd. plans to execute the concerned merger. No shares will be issued, no
increase in capital will be made, and no cash will be paid to Komatsu Rental.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">4) Treatment of stock acquisition rights and bonds with stock acquisition rights in relation to
this merger
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Not applicable.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><U>4. Status of the Listed Company after the Absorption-Type Merger</U>
</DIV>

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="29%">&nbsp;</TD>

    <TD width="70%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<TR></TR>
<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD valign="top"><DIV style="margin-left:0px; text-indent:-0px">1) Corporate name:
</DIV></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="left" valign="top">Komatsu Ltd.</TD>
